description: Components that are deliberately NOT published as content-addressed store entries, with the reason for each. An exclusion that is not written down is an exclusion that lapses silently the next time somebody extends the store, which is how a store acquires a component that corrupts it. `ci/test/windows-store-relocation.ps1` cross-checks this list against env.ps1's own dispatch block, so the two cannot drift.

exclusions.summary: FreePascal is the one component installed by a vendor installer rather than unpacked from an archive, and an installer that writes machine state is the shape an immutable, relocatable store entry cannot hold.
evidence: non-nix-build/windows/ensure-fpc.ps1 downloads `fpc-<version>.win32.and.win64.exe` and runs it with Inno Setup's silent switches (`/VERYSILENT /SP- /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /NOICONS /DIR=<installRoot>/fpc/<version>`). Every other gated component is an archive extraction.

env.ps1's dispatch block declares FPC with `-Relocatability installer`; all other gated components declare `relocatable`. The declaration and the source agree, which is not true of every component (GCC and RUST declared `relocatable` while the filesystem disagreed).
exclusions.cost: Bounded and measured: env.ps1's own per-component decomposition (`windows-env-decomposition.json`, written by Write-BootstrapStepReport) records FPC's wall-clock seconds, bytes and file count on every complete provisioning run, so the price of keeping this component per-job is a number the run itself produces rather than an estimate. Read it there; it is host- and version-dependent and is deliberately not copied into this file, where it would go stale silently.

open_questions.claim: the installer writes uninstall registry keys
open_questions.why_not_measured: Establishing it requires running the Inno Setup installer on a Windows host and diffing HKLM/HKCU. It cannot be established from this repository: a full-tree grep finds no registry reference anywhere under non-nix-build/windows/. It must not be recorded as measured on the strength of Inno Setup's documented general behaviour, because the question is what THIS installer script does, and an installer may set Uninstallable=no.
open_questions.how_to_measure: On a scratch Windows host: capture `reg export HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall before.reg`, run Ensure-Fpc, export again, and diff. Repeat for the 32-bit view (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\...`) and for HKCU.

open_questions.claim: the installer bakes absolute paths into fpc.cfg
open_questions.why_not_measured: Same reason: no fpc.cfg exists in this repository and none is generated by any script here, so the file only comes into existence when the vendor installer runs.
open_questions.how_to_measure: After Ensure-Fpc, run `Get-BakedAbsolutePathFindings -Root <installRoot> -Path <installRoot>/fpc/<version>` (toolchain-utils.ps1). That is the same content scan the relocatability audit uses, and it answers the question directly rather than by inspection.

exclusions.consequence_if_answered: If both answers turn out to be 'no', or if the payload can be extracted without running the installer, FPC becomes a store candidate and this entry should be revisited. Until then the honest answer is that it stays per-job, and the measured cost above is what that answer costs.

exclusions.summary: MSVC is never installed by this bootstrap. It is DISCOVERED, and it is part of the golden image. There is nothing to publish and nothing to relocate, and it is not a per-job cost either.
evidence: non-nix-build/windows/export-msvc-env.ps1 has no download, no extraction and no install step of any kind. It locates vswhere.exe under ProgramFiles(x86), queries `-latest -products * -requires <VC tools component> -property installationPath`, runs vcvarsall.bat in a child cmd.exe, and prints KEY=VALUE lines.
Every failure path calls Exit-NoMsvcEnvironment, which writes a reason to stderr and exits 0 -- absence of MSVC is a supported state, not an error.

MSVC does not appear in env.ps1's Invoke-BootstrapStep dispatch block at all, so it has no relocatability declaration and no decomposition row. Its absence from the store is therefore structural rather than a policy that could lapse.
